# Project retrospective

**Status:** Initial reflection based on the team's account; team review and
additional evidence are still needed.
**Actual project dates:** _Team to confirm_

## What happened

The original planning material described work across four sprints in an
eight-week limit. The team reports that it instead spent about one week building
the project and did not follow that planned sprint cadence. The eight-week
schedule should therefore be treated as an intended plan, not as evidence that
four sprints, sprint reviews, or mid-sprint check-ins took place.

The repository includes a 24-task QA checklist that explicitly describes test
cases to execute, not proof that they passed. Its QA notes also distinguish
historical, separate smoke and role-test runs from a complete verification of
all acceptance flows. See the [acceptance checklist](../../HOPE_ERP_All_Tester_QA/docs/TEST_CASES_ALL_24.md)
and [QA limitations](../../HOPE_ERP_EXECUTABLE_FIX_AND_QA/README.md).

## Reflection

### What went well

The team's account confirms that it built the project in a concentrated
one-week effort. The team should add specific examples of collaboration,
technical progress, or successful outcomes only after agreeing that they
actually occurred.

- **Team-confirmed example(s):** _Add evidence or leave blank until discussed._

### What was difficult

The clearest process gap reported is the difference between the planned
eight-week sprint schedule and the actual one-week, non-sprint work period.
Without a cadence that the team actually followed, planned sprint artifacts
cannot serve as a reliable record of day-to-day progress, blockers, or
re-estimation.

- **Other team-confirmed challenge(s):** _Add examples after discussion._

### What we learned

- Keep plans distinct from completed work and record actual dates.
- For a short project, use a small board and lightweight check-ins that fit the
  time available rather than reporting an unrun multi-week cadence.
- Keep acceptance criteria and test evidence visible so reviewers can
  distinguish implemented behavior from planned or unverified behavior.

These are suggestions for the team to accept, revise, or decline; they are not

| Record blockers with an owner and next step when they arise. | Team to assign | Next check-in, if held | _Pending team discussion_ |
| Add acceptance criteria and actual test evidence to reviewable changes. | Team to assign | Next pull request | _Pending team discussion_ |
| Hold a brief final review and retrospective if the team has time, recording attendance and outcomes accurately. | Team to assign | Next project close | _Pending team discussion_ |
